$comment: THE FROZEN SCORING DENOMINATOR for phase 394's stage-2 dedup lane (D-04/D-16).
Gap-closure rounds MUST NOT mint new members or edit these vectors to re-score:
the whole proof is that this exact table is observed RED with no dedup lane in
existence and green at the end of the phase, with nothing added in between (the
treadmill law). A row that stops catching what its rationale claims is a finding
about the lane, never a reason to move the row.
WHAT A ROW IS. Each row names an INTENT fixture and a suite. The intent is the
text projection of a house-style test document -- its name followed by its ordered
steps, joined by a space -- read out of intents/<file> at test time rather than
written here as a literal. A corpus assembled as a type literal can pin an input no
producer can emit, and a mutation differential then reds only impossible fixtures.
WHY THE SUITE IS COPIED. suite/uat-381-*.yaml are VERBATIM copies of
demo/init/tests/uat-381-*.yaml, which is the suite 393's frozen corpus scores
against, so the two denominators describe the same world. The copy exists because
the demo tree lives in the super-repository, outside this package's repository, so
no test in packages/agent can read it. 393's corpus solved the same problem by
copying the TEXTS into TypeScript; copying the documents is strictly stronger,
because what is copied is still in the producer's own format.
SYNTHETIC SUITE IDENTITIES. dedup-tie-alpha, dedup-tie-beta and
dedup-unfingerprinted carry demo-style workspace-relative identity paths for
members the demo suite does not contain. They exist because two properties have no
home in the real suite: no intent can tie uat-381-ladder against
uat-381-ladder-current-target (their token sets differ by exactly one member, and
the Jaccard denominators differ by one, so equal scores force a shared count of
zero), and the real suite has no member standing for a test the derived
fingerprint index has no rows for.
score/sharedTokens/comparedTests are what textSimilarity ACTUALLY produced over
these documents, measured 2026-08-11 by evaluating the shipped algorithm over the
files themselves. score is written to ten decimal places because the boundary
triple is decided in the fourth.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a near-duplicate intent is refused at all. The document mirrors uat-381-local-form's anchors in cosmetically different wording (Enter/Press for Type/Click, literal values for the env and secret placeholders). If this row admits, the lane does not screen.
rows.measured: 0.5000000000 against uat-381-local-form (15 shared of 21+24), then 0.3667 and 0.3548 against the two ladder members -- the same 0.5 393 measured for this text against this file, because stage 2 and gate 3 read the same rows through the same textSimilarity.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the lane still ADMITS. A threshold that refuses everything passes a refuse-only corpus, so the exclusion leg needs a control leg beside it or 'it refused' is a reading from an instrument that cannot read. This is a genuine near-miss, not a stranger: 0.0333 below the pin.
rows.measured: top score 0.4166666667 against uat-381-ladder (10 shared of 14+20). NOTE the suite-wide reading MOVES this number: 393 measured the same text at 0.4074 because it scored against uat-381-local-form alone. Screening every suite member raises a draft's maximum, which is why the pin cannot be inherited from 393's.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the >= direction. Its score equals the pin to the digit, so a lane written with > admits it and this row is the only one that says so. The document is deliberately minimal -- one name, one step -- because its nine tokens are exactly the nine that land the Jaccard on 9/20.
rows.measured: 0.4500000000 against uat-381-ladder (9 shared of 9+20; all nine intent tokens are ladder tokens). 9/20 and the literal 0.45 are the same IEEE-754 double, so the equality is exact rather than approximate. 0.4285714286 and 0.2222222222 against the other two.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the step immediately BELOW the pin admits. Pairs with at-threshold and above-threshold as the boundary triple; a lane that rounded, clamped or compared at reduced precision would fail here first.
rows.measured: 0.4482758621 against uat-381-local-form (13 shared of 18+24 = 13/29). This is the largest score achievable below 0.45 from the local-form step vocabulary -- 0.0017 under the pin.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the step immediately ABOVE the pin refuses. The other half of the boundary triple. Below and above sit 0.0034 apart around the pin, so the triple pins a point rather than a region.
rows.measured: 0.4516129032 against uat-381-local-form (14 shared of 21+24 = 14/31). Smallest score achievable above 0.45 from the same vocabulary -- 0.0016 over the pin.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: an empty suite admits every intent and reports NO closest match. Deliberately driven by the obvious-duplicate intent, the strongest refusal candidate in the table, so the row says the empty corpus admits it rather than that some weak intent slipped through. The first test a project ever writes must not be refused for resembling nothing.
rows.measured: comparedTests 0, no closest reported, no-duplicate arm. There is no score to record because nothing was compared.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the degenerate 0/0 is not an identity. An empty intent against a suite entry with an empty name and no steps scores 0, not 1. Reading it as 1 would let a single empty corpus entry cover every intent ever screened -- an over-flag so complete the safe direction becomes a lane that always refuses. The rule is INHERITED from textSimilarity's own early return rather than re-derived here; this row is the assertion that dedup did not add a second reading of it.
rows.measured: score 0, no-duplicate. This is the ONE row with no document behind it: the empty intent is not the projection of any test, because a document with no name does not parse. It is the degenerate input, and the corpus says so rather than pretending a fixture produced it.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: tie-break stability. Two suite members score identically, and the refusal must name the lexicographically smallest workspace-relative identity path so two invocations against the same suite report the same duplicate. beta is fed BEFORE alpha on purpose -- a lane that kept natural iteration order, or that used a strict > on the running best, names beta and this row is the only one that notices.
rows.measured: alpha and beta both 0.6363636364 (14 shared of 18+18 = 14/22), bit-identical because their documents carry identical text at different paths. The three real suite members trail at 0.3929/0.3548/0.3103. No intent can tie the two real ladder members -- see the $comment.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the comparison universe is EVERY test in the suite. dedup-unfingerprinted stands for a member the derived fingerprint index has no rows for -- exactly the population gate 3's text lane keeps and gate 3's fingerprint lane drops, and exactly the population a corpus narrowed to the fingerprint-covered subset would lose. The row also pins comparedTests at the full suite size, so a lane that filtered its input reds here on the count before it reds on the match.
rows.measured: 0.7000000000 against dedup-unfingerprinted (14 shared of 17+17), then 0.1935/0.1714/0.1515 against the three real members. comparedTests 4. An intent has no execution fingerprint, so the anchor-sequence recipe cannot fire pre-run -- this is why the pre-run screen must read the suite rather than the index.
